title: WPA Institutional DNA Reuse Layer
purpose: Route verified institutional practices extracted from global Evidence Dossiers into the full WPA Institute ecosystem while preserving provenance, context, source boundaries and human authority.
core_formula: Evidence Dossier -> Institutional Practice Atoms -> Governed Reuse Routes -> Human Gate -> WPA Application -> Outcome Measurement -> Correction -> Knowledge Reintegration
principles: One verified institutional insight may inform multiple WPA domains, but every reuse preserves source provenance and context.
Reuse means learning, comparison, synthesis or adaptation; it does not mean copying proprietary material or presenting another institution's practice as WPA authorship.
Practice Atoms are not scores and do not create institutional endorsement, accreditation or partnership claims.
Agents may identify and propose reuse routes; consequential institutional adoption remains human-governed.
NE, uncertainty, contradiction and source-tier limits follow the atom into every downstream use.
A source-supported practice may trigger a new research question or methodology review even when it does not fit I01-I20.
Commercial or paid activation remains subject to the existing WPA financial/governance freeze.

atom_lifecycle: Extract candidate practice from Evidence Dossier
Classify practice type and I01-I20 links
Measure outcome of WPA application where possible
Correct or withdraw if source/practice changes
Reintegrate validated learning into the WPA knowledge corpus
provenance_minimum: practice summary in WPA's own words
anti_copying_boundary: Do not reproduce proprietary curricula, manuals or substantial protected text.
Do not imply that a practice originated at WPA when it was observed elsewhere.
Do not convert institutional observation into partnership, endorsement or permission claims.
Use abstraction, comparison and attribution rather than replication of protected expression.
success_metrics: percentage of approved Practice Atoms with complete provenance
number of WPA domains benefiting from approved atoms without provenance loss
rate of downstream corrections propagated successfully
percentage of methodology changes traceable to corpus evidence
number of new research/programme questions generated from distinctive practices
